gloss: to be worth; to deserve; to merit

definitions.gloss: to be worth; to deserve; to merit; to be worthy of
definitions.explanation: To have enough value or importance to warrant a particular action, effort, or assessment.

examples.japanese: {読|よ}むに{値|あたい}する{本|ほん}だ。
examples.english: It is a book worth reading.

examples.japanese: この{発見|はっけん}は{注目|ちゅうもく}に{値|あたい}する。
{彼|かれ}の{努力|どりょく}は{称賛|しょうさん}に{値|あたい}するものだった。
examples.english: His efforts were worthy of praise.

notes:
{値|あたい}する is a literary, somewhat formal expression meaning to be worthy of or to merit. It is typically used in the pattern ～に{値|あたい}する (to be worth doing / to deserve). It carries a tone of considered judgment and is common in written Japanese, reviews, and evaluations.

USAGE:
- ～に{値|あたい}する: to be worth ~; to deserve ~
- ～するに{値|あたい}する: to be worth doing ~

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {注目|ちゅうもく}に{値|あたい}する: to be worthy of attention
- {称賛|しょうさん}に{値|あたい}する: to deserve praise
- {信頼|しんらい}に{値|あたい}する: to be trustworthy
- {尊敬|そんけい}に{値|あたい}する: to be worthy of respect
- {一読|いちどく}に{値|あたい}する: to be worth a read

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ～に{足|た}る: to be worthy of; to be sufficient — very close synonym, slightly more literary
- ふさわしい: suitable; worthy — describes general suitability rather than merit-based worthiness
- ～{甲斐|がい}がある: to be worth doing — more colloquial, emphasizes the reward felt after effort

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {値|あたい}していませんでした
